title.raw: 卷三十九 蜀書九 董劉馬陳董呂傳 Volume 39: Book of Shu 9 - Biographies of Dong, Liu, Ma, Chen, Dong, and Lü

sentences.zh: 董和字幼宰，南郡枝江人也，其先本巴郡江州人。

translations.literal: Dong He, courtesy name Youzai, was a man of Zhijiang in Nan Commandery; his ancestors had originally been people of Jiangzhou in Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dong He, styled Youzai, came from Zhijiang in Nan Commandery; his family had originally hailed from Jiangzhou in Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢末，和率宗族西遷，益州牧劉璋以為牛鞞、

translations.literal: At the end of the Han, He led his clan westward in migration, and the Governor of Yi Province, Liu Zhang, appointed him Magistrate of Niupi and
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty neared its end, Dong He moved west with his kinsmen, and Liu Zhang, governor of Yi Province, named him magistrate of Niupi and

sentences.zh: 〈音髀。〉

translations.literal: 〈Pronounced like bi (thigh).〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The place name is read like the word for “thigh.”〉

sentences.zh: 江原長、成都令。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Jiangyuan and Prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: magistrate of Jiangyuan and prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蜀土富實，時俗奢侈，貨殖之家，侯服玉食，婚姻葬送，傾家竭產。

translations.literal: The land of Shu was rich and solid; the customs of the time were extravagant; households that traded and accumulated wealth wore lordly garments and ate fine food; marriages, burials, and send-offs exhausted families and drained estates.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was prosperous, yet people lived lavishly: merchant families dressed like nobles and dined on delicacies, and weddings and funerals could ruin a household overnight.

sentences.zh: 和躬率以儉，惡衣蔬食，防遏逾僭，為之軌制，所在皆移風變善，畏而不犯。

translations.literal: He personally led by economy in coarse clothing and plain food, guarded against excess and usurpation, and for them established norms and regulations; everywhere customs shifted and turned good; they feared and did not transgress.
translations.idiomatic: Dong He set the tone himself with plain clothes and simple fare, curbing extravagance and overstepping by fixed rules, so that wherever he served manners improved and people stayed within bounds out of respect.

sentences.zh: 然縣界豪強憚和嚴法，說璋轉和為巴東屬國都尉。

translations.literal: Yet the powerful families within the county boundaries feared He’s strict laws and persuaded Zhang to transfer He to be Commandant of the Dependent State of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Local magnates, chafing under his strict enforcement, talked Liu Zhang into moving him to commandant of the dependent state attached to Badong.

sentences.zh: 吏民老弱相攜乞留和者數千人，璋聽留二年，還遷益州太守，其清約如前。

translations.literal: Officials and common people, old and weak, supporting one another, begged to retain He—several thousand; Zhang listened and allowed him to stay two years, then promoted him again to Governor of Yi Province, his cleanness and restraint as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of officials and townsfolk, young and old, pleaded together that he stay; Liu Zhang let him remain two years more, then restored him as governor of Yi Province, and he was as frugal and upright as ever.

sentences.zh: 與蠻夷從事，務推誠心，南土愛而信之。

translations.literal: In dealing with the Man and Yi tribes, he strove to extend sincere heart; the southern lands loved and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: In his work with the southern tribes he relied on good faith, and the region came to love and trust him.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀，徵和為掌軍中郎將，與軍師將軍諸葛亮並署左將軍大司馬府事，獻可替否，共為歡交。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord pacified Shu, he summoned He as General of the Household Who Handles the Army, and together with General of the Military Advisers Zhuge Liang jointly managed the affairs of the Left General and Grand Marshal’s office; they presented what was acceptable and replaced what was not, and together formed a bond of happy friendship.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei took Shu, Dong He was called up as a general of the household for army affairs; he and Military Adviser General Zhuge Liang jointly ran the Left General–Grand Marshal headquarters, candidly offering counsel and enjoying genuine rapport.

sentences.zh: 自和居官食祿，外牧殊域，內幹機衡，二十馀年，死之日家無儋石之財。

translations.literal: From the time He held office and ate salary, outwardly shepherding remote regions, inwardly managing the pivots and scales, more than twenty years, on the day he died his household had not a dan or shi of wealth.
translations.idiomatic: For over twenty years he served abroad on the frontier and at home at the center of government, yet when he died his family still owned scarcely a sack of grain.

sentences.zh: 亮後為丞相，教與群下曰：「夫參署者，集眾思廣忠益也。

translations.literal: Later, when Liang became Chancellor, he instructed the host of subordinates, saying, “As for joint administration, it gathers many thoughts and broadens loyal benefit.”
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang later became chancellor, he taught his subordinates that shared office was meant to collect many views and broaden loyal, beneficial advice.

sentences.zh: 若遠小嫌，難相違覆，曠闕損矣。

translations.literal: If one keeps distant small resentments, it is hard mutually to oppose and review; negligence and loss result.
translations.idiomatic: If people nurse petty slights and shy away from challenging one another’s views, things fall through the cracks and the realm suffers.

sentences.zh: 違覆而得中，猶棄弊蹻而獲珠玉。

translations.literal: Opposing and reviewing and thereby hitting the center is like casting aside worn straw sandals and obtaining pearls and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Frank exchange that lands on the right course is like trading tattered sandals for pearls and jade.

sentences.zh: 然人心苦不能盡，惟徐元直處茲不惑，又董幼宰參署七年，事有不至，至於十反，來相啟告。

translations.literal: Yet people’s hearts bitterly cannot exhaust it; only Xu Yuanzhi in this was not confused; moreover Dong Youzai participated in joint administration seven years; when matters did not arrive, as many as ten times he returned to inform and report.
translations.idiomatic: Few can bring themselves to go that far—only Xu Shu stayed clearheaded here; Dong Youzai served seven years in joint administration and, whenever something was overlooked, came back as many as ten times to set the record straight.

sentences.zh: 苟能慕元直之十一，幼宰之殷勤，有忠於國，則亮可少過矣。

translations.literal: If one could emulate Yuanzhi’s one tenth, Youzai’s earnest diligence, and have loyalty to the state, then Liang could have fewer faults.
translations.idiomatic: If others could show even a fraction of Xu Shu’s steadiness and Dong Youzai’s persistence in serving the state, I would make far fewer mistakes of my own.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「昔初交州平，屢聞得失，後交元直，勤見啟誨，前參事於幼宰，每言則盡，後從事於偉度，數有諫止；

translations.literal: He also said, “In the past, when I first befriended Zhouping, I repeatedly heard of gains and losses; afterward I befriended Yuanzhi, who diligently showed enlightenment and instruction; before I assisted in affairs with Youzai, each time he spoke he exhausted his words; afterward I followed service with Weidu, and several times there were remonstrations and stops;
translations.idiomatic: He added that when he first knew Zhouping he constantly learned what worked and what failed; Xu Shu then instructed him tirelessly; whenever he worked with Dong Youzai the man held nothing back; and Hu Weidu later checked him whenever he went astray;

sentences.zh: 雖姿性鄙暗，不能悉納，然與此四子終始好合，亦足以明其不疑於直言也。

translations.literal: Although my nature is base and dim and I could not wholly accept, yet with these four men from beginning to end we were harmoniously joined; this also suffices to clarify that I did not doubt straight speech.”
translations.idiomatic: Dull and stubborn as I was, I could not embrace every proposal, yet I kept faith with all four to the end—enough to show I never shrank from blunt counsel.”

sentences.zh: 」其追思和如此。

translations.literal: ” His recollective longing for He was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard in which Zhuge Liang held Dong He.

sentences.zh: 〈偉度者，姓胡，名濟，義陽人。

translations.literal: 〈Weidu—surname Hu, given name Ji, a man of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Hu Ji, styled Weidu, was from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 為亮主簿，有忠藎之效，故見褒述。

translations.literal: He was Liang’s chief clerk and had the effect of loyal devotion; therefore he was praised and described.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Zhuge Liang’s chief clerk with conspicuous loyalty, which is why the text singles him out for praise.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，為中典軍，統諸軍，封成陽亭侯，遷中監軍前將軍，督漢中，假節領兗州刺史，至右驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Liang died, he became Central Army Director-in-Chief, commanding the various armies, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengyang village, was promoted to Front General who Supervises the Army, supervised Hanzhong, was granted insignia and concurrent Inspector of Yan Province, reaching General of the Right Cavalry on the Fast Attack.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang’s death he rose through central army posts, took command of the forces, was made village marquis of Chengyang, advanced to front general and army supervisor for Hanzhong, carried imperial credentials with titular authority over Yan Province, and ended as senior general of the right wing.

sentences.zh: 濟弟博，歷長水校尉尚書。〉

translations.literal: Ji’s younger brother Bo successively served as Colonel of the Chang River Regiment and Minister.〉
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hu Bo became colonel of the Chang River regiment and a minister of state.〉

sentences.zh: 劉巴字子初，零陵烝陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ba, courtesy name Zichu, was a man of Zhengyang in Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba, styled Zichu, came from Zhengyang in Lingling commandery.

sentences.zh: 少知名，

translations.literal: In youth he was known.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he was widely known.

sentences.zh: 〈零陵先賢傳曰：巴祖父曜，蒼梧太守。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of Lingling states: Ba’s grandfather Yao was Governor of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈According to the Traditions of Worthies of Lingling, his grandfather Liu Yao had been governor of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 父祥，江夏太守、蕩寇將軍。

translations.literal: His father Xiang was Governor of Jiangxia and General Who Sweeps Away Brigands.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Xiang held Jiangxia and the title General Who Sweeps Away Brigands.

sentences.zh: 時孫堅舉兵討董卓，以南陽太守張諮不給軍糧，殺之。

translations.literal: At the time Sun Jian raised troops to attack Dong Zhuo; because the Governor of Nanyang, Zhang Zi, did not supply army grain, he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian marched against Dong Zhuo, he executed Nanyang governor Zhang Zi for withholding supplies.

sentences.zh: 祥與同心，南陽士民由此怨祥，舉兵攻之，與戰，敗亡。

translations.literal: Xiang was of one heart with him; Nanyang gentlemen and common people therefore resented Xiang, raised troops and attacked him; they battled and were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang had sided with Sun Jian, so the people of Nanyang turned on him, took up arms, and drove him out in defeat.

sentences.zh: 劉表亦素不善祥，拘巴，欲殺之，數遣祥故所親信人密詐謂巴曰：「劉牧欲相危害，可相隨逃之。

translations.literal: Liu Biao also was not on good terms with Xiang; he detained Ba and wished to kill him; several times he sent Xiang’s former trusted intimates secretly to deceive Ba, saying, “Governor Liu wishes mutually to harm and endanger you; you can flee together with us.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao had long distrusted Liu Xiang and held Liu Ba hostage, intending to execute him; he repeatedly sent men Liu Xiang had trusted to lure the boy with false warnings that “the governor means you harm—come away with us.”

sentences.zh: 」如此再三，巴輒不應。

translations.literal: ” Like this again thrice; Ba each time did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: They tried several times; Liu Ba refused each overture.

sentences.zh: 具以報表，表乃不殺巴。

translations.literal: He reported everything in full to Biao; Biao then did not kill Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba reported the whole ruse to Liu Biao, who then spared him.

sentences.zh: 年十八，郡署戶曹史主記主簿。

translations.literal: At age eighteen, the commandery appointed him Clerk of the Household Bureau, Recorder-in-Chief, and chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen the commandery put him on staff as household registrar, master of records, and chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 劉先

translations.literal: Liu Xian
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian

translations.literal: (host)
translations.idiomatic: 〈manuscript note: “host”〉

sentences.zh: 欲遣週不疑就巴學，巴答曰：「昔遊荊北，時涉師門，記問之學，不足紀名，內無楊硃守靜之術，外無墨翟務時之風，猶天之南箕，虛而不用。

translations.literal: Liu Xian wished to send Zhou Buyi to study with Ba; Ba replied, saying, “In the past I wandered north of Jing and at times crossed teachers’ gates; learning of memorization and questioning is not sufficient to record a name; inwardly I lack Yang Zhu’s art of guarding quiet; outwardly I lack Mozi’s wind of attending to the times; I am like the Southern Dipper in the sky—empty and unused.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian wished to send the prodigy Zhou Buyi to study under him. Liu Ba declined: “My schooling in the north of Jing was mere cramming for exams—I have neither Yang Zhu’s inward discipline nor Mozi’s practical drive; I would be the hollow Southern Dipper, bright in the sky but useless on earth.”

sentences.zh: 賜書乃欲令賢甥摧鸞鳳之艷，遊燕雀之宇，將何以啟明之哉？

translations.literal: Your granted letter then wishes to make your worthy nephew destroy the splendor of simurgh and phoenix and roam the house of swallows and sparrows—how will you enlighten him?”
translations.idiomatic: You would have your brilliant nephew clip phoenix wings to flutter among sparrows—how could that enlighten him?”

sentences.zh: 愧於‘有若無，實若虛’，何以堪之！」〉

translations.literal: I am ashamed before ‘having as if not having, full as if empty’—how can I bear it!”〉
translations.idiomatic: I fall short of the Master’s ‘to seem empty though full’—how could I face such a pupil!”〉

sentences.zh: 荊州牧劉表連闢，及舉茂才，皆不就。

translations.literal: The Governor of Jing Province, Liu Biao, repeatedly summoned him, and nominated him as Flourishing Talent; he did not go to any.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao summoned him repeatedly and nominated him as a “flourishing talent,” but Liu Ba never accepted.

sentences.zh: 表卒，曹公徵荊州。

translations.literal: When Biao died, Duke Cao campaigned against Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Biao died, Cao Cao marched on Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 先主奔江南，荊、楚群士從之如雲，而巴北詣曹公。

translations.literal: The Former Lord fled to Jiangnan; the host of gentlemen of Jing and Chu followed him like clouds, but Ba went north to Duke Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei fled south while talent from Jing and Chu flocked to him—yet Liu Ba went north to join Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 曹公闢為掾，使招納長沙、零陵、桂陽。

translations.literal: Duke Cao summoned him as an aide and ordered him to summon and receive Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao appointed him an aide and sent him to win over Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 〈零陵先賢傳曰：曹公敗於烏林，還北時，欲遣桓階，階辭不如巴。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of Lingling states: When Duke Cao was defeated at Wulin, when returning north he wished to send Huan Jie; Jie declined, saying he was not as good as Ba.
translations.idiomatic: 〈After Cao Cao’s defeat at Wulin he planned to send Huan Jie north; Huan Jie said Liu Ba was the better man.

sentences.zh: 巴謂曹公曰：「劉備據荊州，不可也。

translations.literal: Ba said to Duke Cao, “Liu Bei occupying Jing Province—this cannot be.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba warned Cao Cao, “You cannot leave Liu Bei holding Jing Province.”

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「備如相圖，孤以六軍繼之也。」〉

translations.literal: ” The Duke said, “If Bei plots against me, I with the Six Armies will follow him.”〉
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied, “If he turns on me, I will bring the host down on him.”〉

sentences.zh: 會先主略有三郡，巴不得反使，遂遠適交阯，

translations.literal: It happened that the Former Lord seized roughly three commanderies; Ba could not return on his mission, and therefore went far to remove to Jiaozhi,
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei then seized three commanderies, blocking Liu Ba’s return to Cao Cao’s camp, so he fled far south toward Jiaozhi,

sentences.zh: 〈零陵先賢傳云：巴往零陵，事不成，欲遊交州，道還京師。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of Lingling states: Ba went to Lingling; the affair did not succeed; he wished to travel to Jiao Province and by the road return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Another note says he tried Lingling first, then meant to cross into Jiao Province and make his way back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛亮在臨烝，巴與亮書曰：「乘危歷險，到值思義之民，自與之眾，承天之心，順物之性，非餘身謀所能勸動。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuge Liang was at Linzheng; Ba wrote a letter to Liang, saying, “Riding peril and traversing danger, arriving to encounter people who think of righteousness, aligning with their masses, inheriting Heaven’s heart, complying with things’ nature—this is not something my personal schemes can urge or move.”
translations.idiomatic: From Linzheng, Zhuge Liang received a letter: “I have crossed danger to reach people moved by duty; their gathering follows heaven’s intent and human nature—no private scheme of mine could sway them.”

sentences.zh: 若道窮數盡，將託命於滄海，不復顧荊州矣。

translations.literal: If the way is exhausted and the reckoning ends, I will entrust my fate to the vast sea and will not again look toward Jing Province.”
translations.idiomatic: If every road closes, I will trust my life to the open sea and never trouble Jing Province again.”

sentences.zh: 」亮追謂曰：「劉公雄才蓋世，據有荊土，莫不歸德，天人去就，已可知矣。

translations.literal: ” Liang pursued with words, saying, “Lord Liu’s heroic talent covers the age; he occupies Jing territory; none do not return virtue; Heaven and men’s going and staying—already can be known.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang wrote back: “Liu Bei’s gifts tower above his age; he holds the Jing heartland and commands loyalty—Heaven’s choice is plain.”

sentences.zh: 足下欲何之？

translations.literal: Where do you wish to go?”
translations.idiomatic: Where else could you possibly go?”

sentences.zh: 」巴曰：「受命而來，不成當還，此其宜也。

translations.literal: ” Ba said, “I came bearing orders; if it does not succeed I ought to return—this is its propriety.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba answered, “I came under orders; if I fail I should report back—that is only proper.”

sentences.zh: 足下何言邪！」〉

translations.literal: What are you saying, sir!”〉
translations.idiomatic: What are you talking about?”〉

sentences.zh: 先主深以為恨。

translations.literal: The Former Lord deeply took this as resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei nursed a deep grudge over it.

sentences.zh: 巴復從交阯至蜀。

translations.literal: Ba again went from Jiaozhi to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba eventually traveled from Jiaozhi into Shu.

sentences.zh: 〈零陵先賢傳曰：巴入交阯，更姓為張。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of Lingling states: Ba entered Jiaozhi and changed his surname to Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: 〈To hide in the south he entered Jiaozhi under the surname Zhang.

sentences.zh: 與交阯太守士谿計議不合，乃由牂牁道去。

translations.literal: With the Governor of Jiaozhi, Shi Xi, plans and discussions did not agree; then he departed by the Zangke road.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with Jiaozhi governor Shi Xi and slipped away along the Zangke route.

sentences.zh: 為益州郡所拘留，太守欲殺之。

translations.literal: He was detained by Yi Province Commandery; the governor wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Province commandery seized him and the local governor meant to execute him.

sentences.zh: 主簿曰：「此非常人，不可殺也。

translations.literal: The chief clerk said, “This is not an ordinary person; he cannot be killed.”
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk protested, “This man is no ordinary captive.”

sentences.zh: 」主簿請自送至州，見益州牧劉璋，璋父焉昔為巴父祥所舉孝廉，見巴驚喜，每大事輒以諮訪。

translations.literal: ” The chief clerk requested personally to escort him to the province; seeing the Governor of Yi Province, Liu Zhang—Zhang’s father Yan in the past had been nominated Filial and Incorrupt by Ba’s father Xiang—seeing Ba was surprised and delighted; on each great matter he then consulted and inquired.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded the governor to send him up to Liu Zhang: Liu Yan had once received his “filial and incorrupt” nomination from Liu Ba’s father, so Zhang welcomed him eagerly and sought his counsel on weighty affairs.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：劉焉在漢靈帝時已經宗正太常，出為益州牧，祥始以孫堅作長沙時為江夏太守，不得舉焉為孝廉，明也。〉

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi examines: Liu Yan in Emperor Ling of Han’s time had already been Director of the Imperial Clan and Grand Master of Ceremonies; he went out as Governor of Yi Province; Xiang only when Sun Jian was acting as Changsha was Governor of Jiangxia—he could not have nominated Yan as Filial and Incorrupt; this is clear.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Liu Yan was already grand master of ceremonies under Emperor Ling before he became governor of Yi, while Liu Xiang did not become governor of Jiangxia until Sun Jian’s Changsha days—so Xiang could not have nominated Liu Yan as filial and incorrupt; the anecdote is impossible.〉

sentences.zh: 俄而先主定益州，巴辭謝罪負，先主不責。

translations.literal: Soon the Former Lord pacified Yi Province; Ba apologized for guilt and fault; the Former Lord did not blame.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei took Yi Province, Liu Ba offered a humble apology for his past disloyalty; Liu Bei did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 〈零陵先賢傳曰：璋遣法正迎劉備，巴諫曰：「備，雄人也，入必為害，不可內也。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of Lingling states: Zhang sent Fa Zheng to welcome Liu Bei; Ba remonstrated, saying, “Bei is a heroic man; if he enters he will certainly become harm; he cannot be let in.”
translations.idiomatic: 〈Earlier, when Liu Zhang sent Fa Zheng to invite Liu Bei, Liu Ba warned, “Liu Bei is a conqueror; admit him and he will devour you.”

sentences.zh: 」既入，巴复諫曰：「若使備討張魯，是放虎於山林也。

translations.literal: ” After he entered, Ba again remonstrated, saying, “If you send Bei to attack Zhang Lu, this is releasing a tiger in mountain forests.”
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei crossed the border he urged again, “Sending him against Zhang Lu is like releasing a tiger into the hills.”

sentences.zh: 」璋不聽。

translations.literal: ” Zhang did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang ignored him.

sentences.zh: 巴閉門稱疾。

translations.literal: Ba closed his gate and claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba shut his gates and feigned illness.

sentences.zh: 備攻成都，令軍中曰：「其有害巴者，誅及三族。

translations.literal: When Bei attacked Chengdu, he ordered the army, saying, “Whoever harms Ba—execute extending to three clans.”
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei besieged Chengdu he ordered that anyone who harmed Liu Ba would die with his whole clan.

sentences.zh: 」及得巴，甚喜。〉

translations.literal: ” When he obtained Ba, he was greatly pleased.〉
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ba finally came in, Liu Bei was overjoyed.〉

sentences.zh: 而諸葛孔明數稱薦之，先主闢為左將軍西曹掾。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhuge Kongming repeatedly praised and recommended him; the Former Lord summoned him as Western Bureau Clerk of the Left General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang kept recommending him, and Liu Bei appointed him to the Left General’s western bureau.

sentences.zh: 〈零陵先賢傳曰：張飛嘗就巴宿，巴不與語，飛遂忿恚。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of Lingling states: Zhang Fei once went to Ba’s lodging to stay the night; Ba did not speak with him; Fei then was angry and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhang Fei once tried to spend the night under Liu Ba’s roof; Liu Ba refused to speak to him, and Zhang Fei boiled over.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮謂巴曰：「張飛雖實武人，敬慕足下。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang said to Ba, “Zhang Fei although truly a military man, respects and admires you, sir.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang urged Liu Ba, “Zhang Fei is a soldier, but he admires you.”

sentences.zh: 主公今方收合文武，以定大事；

translations.literal: The lord now is just gathering civil and military to settle the great affair;
translations.idiomatic: Our lord is pulling scholars and generals together for the great enterprise;

sentences.zh: 足下雖天素高亮，宜少降意也。

translations.literal: although you, sir, by heaven’s nature are lofty and bright, you ought slightly to lower your intent.”
translations.idiomatic: however proud your nature, bend a little toward him.”

sentences.zh: 」巴曰：「大丈夫處世，當交四海英雄，如何與兵子共語乎？

translations.literal: ” Ba said, “A great man in his generation ought to befriend heroes of the four seas—how can he speak together with a soldier’s son?”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba replied, “A true man befriends heroes of the realm—why should he banter with some rough camp follower?”

sentences.zh: 」備聞之，怒曰：「孤欲定天下，而子初專亂之。

translations.literal: ” When Bei heard it, he angrily said, “I wish to settle the Under Heaven, yet Zichu specially throws it into disorder.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei heard and thundered, “I mean to settle the realm, and Zichu alone stirs chaos.”

sentences.zh: 其欲還北，假道於此，豈欲成孤事邪？

translations.literal: Does he wish to return north, borrowing a road here—does he wish to complete my affair?”
translations.idiomatic: Does he still mean to bolt north and only pass through my land—does he think that helps me?”

sentences.zh: 」備又曰：「子初才智絕人，如孤，可任用之，非孤者難獨任也。

translations.literal: ” Bei also said, “Zichu’s talent and wisdom surpass others; one like me can employ him; one not like me finds it hard to employ him alone.”
translations.idiomatic: Then he added, “Zichu’s genius stands apart—only someone with my stature can use him; lesser men could never manage him alone.”

sentences.zh: 」亮亦曰：「運籌策於帷幄之中，吾不如子初遠矣！

translations.literal: ” Liang also said, “In plotting strategies within the tent’s curtain, I am far inferior to Zichu!”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang added, “For counsel within the tent I am nowhere near Zichu!”

sentences.zh: 若提枹鼓，會軍門，使百姓喜勇，當與人議之耳。

translations.literal: If one lifts drumsticks and drums and meets at the army gate, causing the hundred surnames to rejoice in bravery—that ought to be discussed with others.”
translations.idiomatic: If the task is to drum at the gate and stir the people to valor, that is for someone else to handle.”

sentences.zh: 」初攻劉璋，備與士眾約：「若事定，府庫百物，孤無預焉。

translations.literal: ” When first attacking Liu Zhang, Bei covenanted with officers and masses: “If the affair is settled, the treasury’s hundred things—I have no part.”
translations.idiomatic: Before the campaign against Liu Zhang, Liu Bei had promised his army, “When Chengdu falls, the treasury is yours—I claim nothing.”

sentences.zh: 」及拔成都，士眾皆舍干戈，赴諸藏競取寶物。

translations.literal: ” When Chengdu was taken, officers and masses all cast aside shields and halberds and rushed to the various storehouses competing to take precious goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the men threw down their weapons and looted every warehouse.

sentences.zh: 軍用不足，備甚憂之。

translations.literal: Army use was insufficient; Bei was greatly worried about it.
translations.idiomatic: The army soon ran short of funds, and Liu Bei despaired.

sentences.zh: 巴曰：「易耳，但當鑄直百錢，平諸物賈，令吏為官巿。

translations.literal: Ba said, “It is easy; only need cast straight-hundred cash, level the prices of the various goods, order clerks to make official markets.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba said, “That is simple: mint hundred-cash coins, stabilize prices, and let officials run public markets.”

sentences.zh: 」備從之，數月之間，府庫充實。〉

translations.literal: ” Bei followed it; within several months the treasury was full and solid.〉
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei agreed; within months the coffers were full again.〉

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年，先主為漢中王，巴為尚書，後代法正為尚書令。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian’an, the Former Lord became King of Hanzhong; Ba was Minister; afterward he replaced Fa Zheng as Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In 219 Liu Bei became king of Hanzhong; Liu Ba served as minister of state and later succeeded Fa Zheng as director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 躬履清儉，不治產業，又自以歸附非素，懼見猜嫌，恭默守靜，退無私交，非公事不言。

translations.literal: He personally practiced purity and frugality, did not manage estates and industries; moreover he himself because submission was not of long standing feared being suspected and resented; respectfully silent he guarded quiet; in retirement he had no private friendships; except for public affairs he did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly and amassed no estate; because he had joined Liu Bei late he feared suspicion, kept his silence, avoided private friendships, and spoke only on official business.

sentences.zh: 〈零陵先賢傳曰：是時中夏人情未一，聞備在蜀，四方延頸。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of Lingling states: At this time the Central Plain’s people’s hearts were not one; hearing Bei was in Shu, the four directions stretched necks.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The heartland was still divided; when word spread that Liu Bei held Shu, hopeful men everywhere watched him.

sentences.zh: 而備銳意欲即真，巴以為如此示天下不廣，且欲緩之。

translations.literal: Yet Bei’s keen intent wished to mount the true throne immediately; Ba thought that like this showed the Under Heaven was not broad, and wished moreover to slow it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was impatient to take the throne; Liu Ba argued that haste would look small-minded to the empire and urged delay.

sentences.zh: 與主簿雍茂諫備，備以他事殺茂，由是遠人不復至矣。〉

translations.literal: Together with chief clerk Yong Mao he remonstrated Bei; Bei on another matter killed Mao; because of this distant people did not again arrive.〉
translations.idiomatic: He and chief clerk Yong Mao spoke against it; Liu Bei later executed Yong on another charge, and talent from afar stopped coming.〉

sentences.zh: 先主稱尊號，昭告於皇天上帝后土神祇，凡諸文誥策命，皆巴所作也。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord assumed the exalted title, he brightly announced to August Heaven, Supreme Emperor, Hou Tu, and the spirits; all documents of edicts, patent letters, and commands were composed by Ba.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei took the imperial title and proclaimed it to Heaven and Earth, Liu Ba drafted every proclamation and patent of appointment.

sentences.zh: 章武二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhangwu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhangwu (222).

sentences.zh: 卒後，魏尚書僕射陳群與丞相諸葛亮書，問巴消息，稱曰劉君子初，甚敬重焉。

translations.literal: After he died, Wei’s Vice Director of the Ministry Chen Qun wrote a letter to Chancellor Zhuge Liang, inquiring after Ba’s news, addressing him as Lord Liu Zichu, greatly respecting him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, Wei’s Chen Qun wrote Zhuge Liang asking news of “Lord Liu Zichu,” with evident esteem.

sentences.zh: 〈零陵先賢傳曰：輔吳將軍張昭嘗對孫權論巴褊□厄，不當拒張飛太甚。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of Lingling states: Auxiliary Wu General Zhang Zhao once before Sun Quan discussed Ba’s narrowness and ill fortune; he ought not to have rejected Zhang Fei too greatly.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhang Zhao once told Sun Quan that Liu Ba’s rigid temper had brought him grief and that he had slighted Zhang Fei too harshly.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「若令子初隨世沈浮，容悅玄德，交非其人，何足稱為高士乎？」〉

translations.literal: Quan said, “If one ordered Zichu to float and sink with the age, please and delight Xuande, associating with not the right people—how could it suffice to be called a lofty gentleman?”〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan replied, “If Liu Ba had flattered Liu Bei and truckled to every faction, could we still call him a gentleman?”〉

sentences.zh: 馬良字季常，襄陽宜城人也。

translations.literal: Ma Liang, courtesy name Jichang, was a man of Yicheng in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang, styled Jichang, was a native of Yicheng in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 兄弟五人，並有才名，鄉里為之諺曰：「馬氏五常，白眉最良。

translations.literal: Five brothers in all, together they had talent and fame; the village and hamlet for them made a proverb, saying, “The Ma clan’s five constants—white eyebrows are the finest.”
translations.idiomatic: Five brothers, all celebrated, inspired a local rhyme: “Among the Ma band of five, the white-browed one thrives.”

sentences.zh: 」良眉中有白毛，故以稱之。

translations.literal: ” Liang in his eyebrows had white hair; therefore by this he was called.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang had white hairs in his brows, hence the nickname.

sentences.zh: 先主領荊州，闢為從事。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord held Jing Province, he summoned him as an attendant clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei governed Jing Province he appointed Ma Liang as an attendant clerk.

sentences.zh: 及先主入蜀，諸葛亮亦從後往，良留荊州，與亮書曰：「聞雒城已拔，此天祚也。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord entered Shu, Zhuge Liang also followed afterward and went; Liang remained in Jing Province, and wrote a letter to Liang, saying, “I hear Luocheng has already been taken; this is Heaven’s blessing.”
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei marched into Shu, Zhuge Liang followed later while Ma Liang stayed behind in Jing; he wrote to Zhuge Liang, “Luocheng has fallen—that is Heaven’s blessing.”

sentences.zh: 尊兄應期贊世，配業光國，魄兆見矣。

translations.literal: Your honoured elder brother responds to the period and aids the age, matching enterprise and glorifying the state—auguries and omens have appeared.”
translations.idiomatic: You have risen with the times to aid the age; your service magnifies the state—and every auspicious sign is already plain.”

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以為良蓋與亮結為兄弟，或相與有親；

translations.literal: 〈Your subject Songzhi thinks that Ma Liang probably with Zhuge Liang became sworn brothers, or perhaps they were kin by marriage;
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi believed that Ma Liang had likely sworn brotherhood with Zhuge Liang, or that the two families were connected by marriage;

sentences.zh: 亮年長，良故呼亮為尊兄耳。〉

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang was the elder; Ma Liang therefore called him honoured elder brother.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was the elder, so Ma Liang addressed him as “honoured elder brother.”〉

sentences.zh: 夫變用雅慮，審貴垂明，於以簡才，宜適其時。

translations.literal: As for applying change with refined thought, examining what is precious and setting forth clarity, thereby to select talent, one should fit the timely moment.
translations.idiomatic: To shift policy with careful judgment, weigh what truly matters, and bring it to light is how one chooses men for the hour.

sentences.zh: 若乃和光悅遠，邁德天壤，使時閒於聽，世服於道，齊高妙之音，正鄭、衛之聲，並利於事，無相奪倫，此乃管弦之至，牙、曠之調也。

translations.literal: If then one blends radiance and pleases the distant, strides virtue between Heaven and earth, causes the age to be leisurely in listening, the generation to submit to the Way, aligns lofty and subtle tones, corrects the sounds of Zheng and Wei, both benefiting affairs without mutually usurping order—this is the utmost of pipes and strings, the tuning of Ya and Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: When ruler and minister move in concert, virtue spans heaven and earth, the age hears clearly and the world trusts the Way; sublime music harmonizes with the reform of vulgar song, every part serves the whole without breaking rank—that is the perfection Boya and Shi Kuang pursued.

sentences.zh: 雖非鍾期，敢不擊節！

translations.literal: Although I am not Zhong Qi, how dare I not beat the measure!
translations.idiomatic: I am no Zhong Ziqi, yet how could I withhold my applause!”

sentences.zh: 」先主闢良為左將軍掾。

translations.literal: ” The Former Lord summoned Liang as an aide to the Left General.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord then appointed Ma Liang as an aide to the Left General.

sentences.zh: 後遣使吳，良謂亮曰：「今銜國命，協穆二家，幸為良介於孫將軍。

translations.literal: Later he sent him as envoy to Wu; Liang said to Liang, “Now I bear the state’s charge to harmonize the two houses; I hope you will be a good go-between for me with General Sun.”
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Bei sent Ma Liang as envoy to Wu. Ma Liang told Zhuge Liang, “I carry an imperial mandate to reconcile our two courts; please speak well of me to General Sun.”

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「君試自為文。

translations.literal: ” Liang said, “You try yourself to compose the document.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang replied, “Draft the memorial yourself.”

sentences.zh: 」良即為草曰：「寡君遣掾馬良通聘繼好，以紹昆吾、豕韋之勳。

translations.literal: ” Liang at once drafted, saying, “My lord sends his aide Ma Liang to open communication and renew friendship, to continue the achievements of Kunwu and Shiwei.”
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang wrote at once: “My lord dispatches his aide Ma Liang to renew friendship and envoys, echoing the ancient deeds of Kunwu and Shiwei.”

sentences.zh: 其人吉士，荊楚之令，鮮于造次之華，而有克終之美，原降心存納，以慰將命。

translations.literal: This man is a good scholar, the finest of Jing and Chu, sparing of hasty flourish yet possessing the beauty of seeing things through; I beg you lower your heart to receive him, to comfort the charge of the envoy.”
translations.idiomatic: He is an honourable man and the pick of Jing and Chu—little given to empty sparkle, yet steadfast to the end; I pray you take him to heart and satisfy the trust of his mission.”

sentences.zh: 」權敬待之。

translations.literal: ” Quan respectfully received him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan received him with due honour.

sentences.zh: 先主稱尊號，以良為侍中。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord assumed the exalted title, he made Liang Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei took the imperial title, he named Ma Liang palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 及東征吳，遣良入武陵招納五溪蠻夷，蠻夷渠帥皆受印號，咸如意指。

translations.literal: When he campaigned east against Wu, he sent Liang into Wuling to summon and receive the Five Streams Man and Yi; the Man and Yi chieftains all received seals and titles, all as his intention directed.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern campaign against Wu, Liu Bei sent Ma Liang into Wuling to win over the Five Streams tribes; every chieftain accepted a seal and obeyed his instructions.

sentences.zh: 會先主敗績於夷陵，良亦遇害。

translations.literal: It happened that the Former Lord suffered defeat at Yiling; Liang also met harm and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei was routed at Yiling, Ma Liang fell with him.

sentences.zh: 先主拜良子秉為騎都尉。

translations.literal: The Former Lord appointed Liang’s son Bing as Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei enfeoffed Ma Liang’s son Ma Bing as commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 良弟謖，字幼常，以荊州從事隨先主入蜀，除綿竹成都令、越雋太守。

translations.literal: Liang’s younger brother Su, courtesy name Youchang, as a clerk of Jing Province followed the Former Lord into Shu, was appointed Prefect of Mianzhu and Chengdu, and Governor of Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang’s younger brother Ma Su, styled Youchang, had entered Shu as a Jing Province clerk and became prefect of Mianzhu and Chengdu and governor of Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 才器過人，好論軍計，丞相諸葛亮深加器異。

translations.literal: His talent and capacity surpassed others; he loved to discuss military plans; Chancellor Zhuge Liang deeply regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His abilities outshone most men’s, he delighted in military debate, and Chancellor Zhuge Liang prized him highly.

sentences.zh: 先主臨薨謂亮曰：「馬謖言過其實，不可大用，君其察之！

translations.literal: When the Former Lord was near death he said to Liang, “Ma Su’s words exceed the reality; he cannot be greatly employed—you must examine this!”
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Liu Bei warned Zhuge Liang, “Ma Su’s reputation outruns his talent—do not give him weighty command; mark my words!”

sentences.zh: 」亮猶謂不然，以謖為參軍，每引見談論，自晝達夜。

translations.literal: ” Liang still thought it was not so; he made Su a staff adviser; every time he summoned him for discussion, from day until night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang disagreed: he kept Ma Su on staff and talked with him from dawn till midnight.

sentences.zh: 〈《襄陽記》曰：建興三年，亮征南中，謖送之數十里。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiangyang Record states: In the third year of Jianxing, Liang campaigned to the south center; Su saw him off for several dozen li.”
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Xiangyang Record notes that in 225 Zhuge Liang marched south and Ma Su accompanied him for miles.”

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「雖共謀之歷年，今可更惠良規。

translations.literal: Liang said, “Although we have planned together for accumulated years, now you may again favour me with good counsel.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang said, “We have schemed together for years—give me one more round of sound advice.”

sentences.zh: 」謖對曰：「南中恃其險遠，不服久矣，雖今日破之，明日復反耳。

translations.literal: ” Su replied, saying, “The south center relies on its rugged distance; it has not submitted for a long time; although today you break it, tomorrow it will rebel again.”
translations.idiomatic: Ma Su answered, “The south trusts its mountains and distance—it has resisted for ages; crush it today and it will rise again tomorrow.”

sentences.zh: 今公方傾國北伐以事強賊。

translations.literal: Now you, sir, are about to tilt the whole state north to campaign against a strong bandit.
translations.idiomatic: You are about to stake the realm on a northern drive against a formidable foe.

sentences.zh: 彼知官勢內虛，其叛亦速。

translations.literal: When they know the court’s power within is empty, their rebellion will also be swift.
translations.idiomatic: Once they sense the capital is drained, they will revolt at once.

sentences.zh: 若殄盡遺類以除後患，既非仁者之情，且又不可倉卒也。

translations.literal: If you exterminate every remaining kind to remove later trouble, that is neither the feeling of the humane one, and moreover cannot be done in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Exterminating every clan to forestall trouble is unworthy of a humane ruler and cannot be rushed besides.”

sentences.zh: 夫用兵之道，攻心為上，攻城為下，心戰為上，兵戰為下，原公服其心而已。

translations.literal: As for the way of employing arms: to attack hearts is best, to attack cities next; heart-warfare is best, soldier-warfare next—I only beg you, sir, subdue their hearts.”
translations.idiomatic: In war, winning hearts comes first and taking cities second; battles of will rank above battles of arms—win their hearts and the south will yield.”

sentences.zh: 」亮納其策，赦孟獲以服南方。

translations.literal: ” Liang adopted his plan, pardoned Meng Huo, and the south submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang took the counsel, spared Meng Huo, and brought the south to heel.

sentences.zh: 故終亮之世，南方不敢復反。〉

translations.literal: Therefore to the end of Liang’s life the south dared not rebel again.〉
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of Zhuge Liang’s life the southern tribes did not rise again.〉

sentences.zh: 建興六年，亮出軍向祁山，時有宿將魏延、吳壹等，論者皆言以為宜令為先鋒，而亮違眾拔謖，統大眾在前，與魏將張郃戰於街亭，為郃所破，士卒離散。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jianxing, Liang led the army out toward Qishan; at the time there were veteran generals Wei Yan, Wu Yi, etc.; commentators all said they thought it fitting to order them as vanguard, but Liang went against the multitude and elevated Su, commanding the great host in front; he fought with Wei general Zhang He at Jieting, was defeated by He, and soldiers scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In 228 Zhuge Liang marched on Qishan. Veteran commanders such as Wei Yan and Wu Yi were available, and opinion favoured them for the van; Zhuge Liang overruled everyone and picked Ma Su to lead the main force. Ma Su met Zhang He at Jieting, was shattered, and his army broke.

sentences.zh: 亮進無所據，退軍還漢中。

translations.literal: Liang advanced with nothing to hold to and withdrew the army to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: With no foothold left, Zhuge Liang pulled back to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 謖下獄物故，亮為之流涕。

translations.literal: Su was cast into prison and died; Liang wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Su died in prison; Zhuge Liang wept for him.

sentences.zh: 良死時年三十六，謖年三十九。

translations.literal: When Liang died he was thirty-six; Su was thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang had died at thirty-six; Ma Su was thirty-nine when he perished.

sentences.zh: 〈襄陽記曰：謖臨終與亮書曰：「明公視謖猶子，謖視明公猶父，原深惟殛鯀興禹之義，使平生之交不虧於此，謖雖死無恨於黃壤也。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiangyang Record states: Su at life’s end wrote to Liang, saying, “The enlightened lord regards Su as a son; Su regards the enlightened lord as a father; I beg you deeply ponder the meaning of executing Gun yet raising Yu, so that our lifelong bond is not marred here—though Su die I have no regret in the yellow earth.”
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Xiangyang Record preserves Ma Su’s last letter: “You have treated me as a son and I have honoured you as a father; recall how Gun was punished yet Yu rose—let our bond survive this shame so that, though I die, I rest easy beneath the yellow springs.”

sentences.zh: 」於時十萬之眾為之垂涕。

translations.literal: ” At that time a host of a hundred thousand for him shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand men wept for him.

sentences.zh: 亮自臨祭，待其遺孤若平生。

translations.literal: Liang personally attended the sacrifice and treated his orphaned children as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang conducted the rites himself and cared for the orphans as though Ma Su still lived.

sentences.zh: 蔣琬後詣漢中，謂亮曰：「昔楚殺得臣，然後文公喜可知也。

translations.literal: Jiang Wan later came to Hanzhong and said to Liang, “In the past Chu killed Dechen; afterward Duke Wen’s joy could be known.”
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan came to Hanzhong and said, “When Chu executed Dechen, Duke Wen of Jin could rejoice at last.”

sentences.zh: 天下未定而戮智計之士，豈不惜乎！

translations.literal: The realm is not yet settled and you execute a man of counsel—is it not regrettable!”
translations.idiomatic: The empire is still unsettled—how can you spare a strategist?”

sentences.zh: 」亮流涕曰：「孫武所以能製勝於天下者，用法明也。

translations.literal: ” Liang said with flowing tears, “The reason Sun Wu could overcome the world was clear use of law.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang answered through tears, “Sun Wu conquered because his law was inexorable.”

sentences.zh: 是以楊乾亂法，魏絳戮其僕。

translations.literal: Therefore when Yang Gan disturbed the law, Wei Jiang executed his servant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Gan broke discipline, Wei Jiang executed his own servant to uphold it.”

sentences.zh: 四海分裂，兵交方始，若復廢法，何用討賊邪！

translations.literal: The four seas are split; arms have barely begun—if we again discard law, what use is striking the rebels!”
translations.idiomatic: The realm is torn and war has barely begun—if we discard the law, how can we defeat Wei?”

sentences.zh: 」習鑿齒曰：諸葛亮之不能兼上國也，豈不宜哉！

translations.literal: ” Xi Zuochi said: Zhuge Liang’s inability to annex the upper states—is it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi commented: Small wonder Zhuge Liang never mastered the Central Plain!”

sentences.zh: 夫晉人規林父之後濟，故廢法而收功；

translations.literal: As for the Jin people’s measuring Lin Fu’s later crossing, therefore they set aside law and gathered merit;
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court watched Xun Lin Fu redeem himself later, bent the statute book, and still won;

sentences.zh: 楚成闇得臣之益己，故殺之以重敗。

translations.literal: King Cheng of Chu was dark to Dechen’s benefiting himself, therefore killed him and doubled defeat.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Chu misread how Dechen helped him, executed him, and doubled his disaster.

sentences.zh: 今蜀僻陋一方，才少上國，而殺其俊傑，退收駑下之用，明法勝才，不師三敗之道，將以成業，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Now Shu is a remote and crude corner; talent is less than the upper state; yet you kill its outstanding men and fall back on employing the mediocre below—law manifestly triumphing over talent, not taking as teacher the way of three defeats—thinking thereby to complete the enterprise—is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Shu is a remote corner with fewer talents than the north; to execute its brightest men and rely on mediocrity—prizing statute over genius while ignoring the lesson of repeated defeat—yet expecting success is folly!”

sentences.zh: 且先主誡謖之不可大用，豈不謂其非才也？

translations.literal: Moreover the Former Lord warned that Su could not be greatly used—did he not mean he was not of talent?
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord warned that Ma Su must not hold high command—was that not a verdict on his talent?

sentences.zh: 亮受誡而不獲奉承，明謖之難廢也。

translations.literal: Liang received the warning yet could not comply and honour it—this clarifies Su’s difficulty to discard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang heard the warning yet could not bring himself to set Ma Su aside—proof of how hard that was.

sentences.zh: 為天下宰匠，欲大收物之力，而不量才節任，隨器付業；

translations.literal: As chief craftsman for the Under Heaven, wishing greatly to gather the strength of things, yet not measuring talent and moderating appointment, assigning tasks according to vessel;
translations.idiomatic: To steward the realm and summon every gift while refusing to match office to ability or assign tasks by measure;

sentences.zh: 知之大過，則違明主之誡，裁之失中，即殺有益之人，難乎其可與言智者也。〉

translations.literal: if knowing errs greatly, then one violates the enlightened lord’s warning; if judgment misses the center, then one kills a beneficial person—hard indeed may one speak of wisdom with such.〉
translations.idiomatic: to misread men that badly defies a dying sovereign’s counsel; to judge wrongly is to destroy the useful—how can we call that wisdom?〉

sentences.zh: 陳震字孝起，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Chen Zhen, courtesy name Xiaoqi, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen, styled Xiaoqi, came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 先主領荊州牧，闢為從事，部諸郡，隨先主入蜀。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord held the governorship of Jing Province, he summoned him as attendant clerk, assigning the various commanderies, and he followed the Former Lord into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Bei governed Jing Province he employed Chen Zhen as an attendant clerk over several commanderies and brought him into Shu.

sentences.zh: 蜀既定，為蜀郡北部都尉，因易郡名，為汶山太守，轉在犍為。

translations.literal: After Shu was settled, he became Northern Commandant of Shu Commandery; because the commandery name was changed, he became Governor of Wenshan, then transferred to be in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest he served as northern commandant of Shu commandery, then—when the jurisdiction was renamed—as governor of Wenshan, and finally transferred to Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 建興三年，入拜尚書，遷尚書令，奉命使吳。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianxing he entered and was appointed Minister, was promoted Director of the Ministry, and received orders to go on mission to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In 225 he entered court as a minister, rose to director of the secretariat, and was sent on embassy to Wu.

sentences.zh: 七年，孫權稱尊號，以震為衛尉，賀權踐阼，諸葛亮與兄瑾書曰：「孝起忠純之性，老而益篤，及其贊述東西，歡樂和合，有可貴者。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Sun Quan assumed the exalted title and made Zhen Commandant of the Guards to congratulate Quan on ascending the throne. Zhuge Liang wrote to elder brother Jin, saying, “Xiaoqi’s loyal and pure nature, old yet more earnest; as for his assisting and narrating east and west, joy and harmony merge—there is much to praise.”
translations.idiomatic: In 229 Sun Quan declared himself emperor and named Chen Zhen minister of the guards to honour his accession. Zhuge Liang wrote to Zhuge Jin: “Xiaoqi’s loyalty has only deepened with age; his work knitting east and west is something to treasure.”

sentences.zh: 」震入吳界，移關候曰：

translations.literal: ” When Zhen entered Wu’s border, he sent notice to the pass officers, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zhen crossed into Wu he notified the border officers:

sentences.zh: 東之與西，驛使往來，冠蓋相望，申盟初好，日新其事。

translations.literal: East and west: relay envoys go back and forth; canopies and covers in sight of one another; extending alliance and early friendship, daily renewing its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: East and west exchange couriers without cease; chariots crowd the roads; the alliance renews itself daily.

sentences.zh: 東尊應保聖祚，告燎受符，剖判土宇，天下響應，各有所歸。

translations.literal: The eastern honourable one fittingly guards the sacred succession, announces at the pyre and receives the tally, divides and partitions territory; Under Heaven responds, each having its return.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern sovereign guards the mandate, performs the great rituals, and maps the realm; the world answers and each side knows its place.

sentences.zh: 於此時也，以同心討賊，則何寇不滅哉！

translations.literal: At this time, with one heart striking the rebels—then what bandit will not be destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: United now against Cao Wei, what enemy could survive?”

sentences.zh: 西朝君臣，引領欣賴。

translations.literal: The western court’s lord and ministers stretch necks in joyful reliance.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu court watches and waits with hope.

sentences.zh: 震以不才，得充下使，奉聘敘好，踐界踴躍，入則如歸。

translations.literal: I, Zhen, lacking talent, have been able to fill the role of humble envoy, bearing friendly mission; crossing the border my heart leaps; entering is like returning home.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy of this mission, yet I bear goodwill across your border with joy and enter as I would my own hall.”

sentences.zh: 獻子適魯，犯其山諱，春秋譏之。

translations.literal: When Xianzi went to Lu he violated their mountain taboo; the Spring and Autumn criticizes it.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn censures Xianzi of Jin for breaking Lu’s taboo on mountain names when he visited.

sentences.zh: 望必啟告，使行人睦焉。

translations.literal: I hope you will surely open and inform, causing the envoy to be harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Please instruct your officers so that envoys may pass without offense.”

sentences.zh: 即日張旍誥眾，各自約誓。

translations.literal: This day spread banners and proclaim to the masses; each binds oath.
translations.idiomatic: This very day we publish the mandate and bind ourselves anew by oath.”

sentences.zh: 順流漂疾，國典異制，懼或有違，幸必斟誨，示其所宜。

translations.literal: Downstream current floats swift; state canons differ in regulation; we fear perhaps some breach; I hope you will surely weigh instruction and show what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The river runs fast and our statutes differ—I fear some breach; I beg your guidance on what is proper.”

sentences.zh: 震到武昌，孫權與震升壇歃盟，交分天下：以徐、豫、幽、青屬吳，並、涼、冀、兗屬蜀，其司州之土，以函谷關為界。

translations.literal: When Zhen reached Wuchang, Sun Quan with Zhen ascended the altar and swore blood alliance, handing over and dividing the Under Heaven: Xu, Yu, You, Qing belong to Wu; Bing, Liang, Ji, Yan belong to Shu; as for Sili Province’s territory, take Hangu Pass as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuchang, Sun Quan joined Chen Zhen on the altar for a blood oath and partitioned the realm: Xu, Yu, You, and Qing went to Wu; Bing, Liang, Ji, and Yan to Shu; the Central Plain itself was split at Hangu Pass.

sentences.zh: 震還，封城陽亭侯。

translations.literal: When Zhen returned, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Chengyang village.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen returned to Shu enfeoffed as village marquis of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 九年，都護李平坐誣罔廢；

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Director of Retainers Li Ping sat for slander and deceit and was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In 231 Director Li Ping was stripped of office for slander;

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮與長史蔣琬、侍中董允書曰：「孝起前臨至吳，為吾說正方腹中有鱗甲，鄉黨以為不可近。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang wrote to Chief Clerk Jiang Wan and Palace Attendant Dong Yun, saying, “When Xiaoqi before went to Wu, he for me said Zhengfang had scales in his belly; his village and hamlet thought him untouchable.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang wrote to Jiang Wan and Dong Yun: “When Chen Zhen last visited Wu he warned me that Li Yan was ‘scaled’—impossible to get close to, say his neighbours.”

sentences.zh: 吾以為鱗甲者但不當犯之耳，不圖復有蘇、張之事出於不意。

translations.literal: I thought scales meant only that one should not offend them—I did not plan again to have Su–Zhang affairs arise beyond expectation.”
translations.idiomatic: I thought that only meant not to provoke him—I never expected another Su Qin or Zhang Yi.”

sentences.zh: 可使孝起知之。

translations.literal: You may cause Xiaoqi to know it.”
translations.idiomatic: Tell Chen Zhen what has happened.”

sentences.zh: 」十三年，震卒。

translations.literal: ” In the thirteenth year Zhen died.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen died in the thirteenth year of Jianxing (235).

sentences.zh: 子濟嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ji inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen Ji inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 董允字休昭，掌軍中郎將和之子也。

translations.literal: Dong Yun, courtesy name Xiuzhao, was the son of General of the Household Who Handles the Army He.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun, styled Xiuzhao, was the son of Dong He, general of the household for army affairs.

sentences.zh: 先主立太子，允以選為捨人，徙洗馬。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord established the heir apparent, Yun by selection became attendant and was transferred to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei named the heir apparent, Dong Yun was chosen as an attendant and soon promoted to junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 後主襲位，遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord succeeded, he was promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shan succeeded, Dong Yun rose to gentleman of the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮將北征，住漢中，慮後主富於春秋，硃紫難別，以允秉心公亮，欲任以宮省之事。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Liang was about to campaign north and stayed in Hanzhong, he worried the Later Lord was rich in spring and autumn years and crimson and purple hard to distinguish; because Yun held a fair and upright heart, he wished to entrust him with palace matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang marched north and stayed in Hanzhong, he feared the young emperor could not tell flattery from counsel; trusting Dong Yun’s fairness, he meant to leave palace affairs in his hands.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「侍中郭攸之、費禕、侍郎董允等，先帝簡拔以遺陛下，至於斟酌規益，進盡忠言，則其任也。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying, “Palace Attendants Guo Youzhi, Fei Yi, Gentleman Dong Yun, etc.—the late emperor selected and raised them for Your Majesty; as for weighing counsel for benefit and advancing full loyal words—that is their charge.”
translations.idiomatic: His memorial named palace attendants Guo Youzhi, Fei Yi, and Dong Yun among others—“men Your Late Father singled out to advise you honestly.”

sentences.zh: 愚以為宮中之事，事無大小，悉以諮之，必能裨補闕漏，有所廣益。

translations.literal: I foolishly think that in palace matters, affairs nothing large or small, consult them all entirely—they can surely remedy omissions and leaks and have broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Consult them on every palace matter, great or small; they will shore up every gap.”

sentences.zh: 若無興德之言，則戮允等以彰其慢。

translations.literal: If there are no words that raise virtue, then execute Yun and the others to expose their slackness.”
translations.idiomatic: If they fail to speak for virtue, punish them to expose their negligence.”

sentences.zh: 」亮尋請禕為參軍，允遷為侍中，領虎賁中郎將，統宿衛親兵。

translations.literal: ” Liang soon requested Yi as staff adviser; Yun was promoted to Palace Attendant, concurrently General of the Household Rapid as Tiger, commanding the inner guard’s close troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang soon pulled Fei Yi onto campaign staff; Dong Yun became palace attendant, led the Rapid-as-Tigers guard, and commanded the imperial bodyguard.”

sentences.zh: 攸之性素和順，備員而已。

translations.literal: Youzhi’s nature was always mild and compliant—he filled a seat only.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Youzhi was mild by nature and little more than a placeholder.

sentences.zh: 〈楚國先賢傳曰：攸之，南陽人，以器業知名於時。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Chu Worthies Traditions states: Youzhi, a man of Nanyang, was known in his time for capacity and enterprise.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Chu Worthies Traditions records Guo Youzhi of Nanyang as a man of recognised talent.〉

sentences.zh: 獻納之任，允皆專之矣。

translations.literal: The duty of presenting and receiving—Yun monopolized it all.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun alone handled frank counsel to the throne.

sentences.zh: 允處事為防制，甚盡匡救之理。

translations.literal: Yun handled affairs with guard and restraint, very fully exhausting the principle of correcting and saving.
translations.idiomatic: He ran court business with tight discipline and laboured to right every wrong.

sentences.zh: 後主常欲採擇以充后宮，允以為古者天子后妃之數不過十二，今嬪嬙已具，不宜增益，終執不聽。

translations.literal: The Later Lord often wished to select and choose to fill the rear palace; Yun thought that in antiquity Son of Heaven’s consorts’ number did not exceed twelve; now concubines and ladies were already complete—should not increase; to the end he held firm and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan often wanted to draft girls for the harem; Dong Yun cited the classical limit of twelve consorts and noted the quarters were already full—he refused every request.

sentences.zh: 後主益嚴憚之。

translations.literal: The Later Lord increasingly sternly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned to fear him even more.

sentences.zh: 尚書令蔣琬領益州刺史，上疏以讓費禕及允，又表「允內侍歷年，翼贊王室，宜賜爵土以褒勳勞。

translations.literal: Director of the Ministry Jiang Wan held concurrently Inspector of Yi Province; he memorialized to yield to Fei Yi and Yun, also stating “Yun has served within for accumulated years, winging and aiding the royal house—should grant title and territory to honour merit and toil.”
translations.idiomatic: Director Jiang Wan, who also governed Yi Province, memorialised to praise Fei Yi and Dong Yun, arguing that Dong Yun’s years of palace service merited a fief.

sentences.zh: 」允固辭不受。

translations.literal: ” Yun firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun steadfastly declined.”

sentences.zh: 後主漸長大，愛宦人黃皓。

translations.literal: The Later Lord gradually grew and loved the eunuch Huang Hao.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Shan matured he grew fond of the eunuch Huang Hao.

sentences.zh: 皓便闢佞慧，欲自容入。

translations.literal: Hao was then clever and fawning, wishing to ingratiate himself to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao flattered cleverly and sought every opening at court.

sentences.zh: 允常上則正色匡主，下則數責於皓。

translations.literal: Yun often above with stern countenance corrected the lord, below repeatedly blamed Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun corrected the emperor to his face and scolded Huang Hao behind the screen.

sentences.zh: 皓畏允，不敢為非。

translations.literal: Hao feared Yun and dared not do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao feared him too much to make trouble.

sentences.zh: 終允之世，皓位不過黃門丞。

translations.literal: To the end of Yun’s life Hao’s rank did not exceed Assistant of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: While Dong Yun lived, Huang Hao never rose above assistant to the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 允嘗與尚書令費禕、中典軍胡濟等共期遊宴，嚴駕已辦，而郎中襄陽董恢詣允脩敬。

translations.literal: Yun once together with Director of the Ministry Fei Yi, Central Army Director Hu Ji, etc., jointly appointed an outing feast; strict carriages were already prepared, but Gentleman Dong Hui of Xiangyang came to Yun to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun once planned an excursion with Fei Yi, Hu Ji, and others; the carriages stood ready when Dong Hui of Xiangyang, a junior gentleman, arrived to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 恢年少官微，見允停出，逡巡求去，允不許，曰：「本所以出者，欲與同好遊談也，今君已自屈，方展闊積，捨此之談，就彼之宴，非所謂也。

translations.literal: Hui was young and low in office; seeing Yun halt departure, he hesitated and sought to leave; Yun did not permit, saying, “Originally the reason for going out was to roam and talk with like-minded friends; now you, sir, have yourself humbled yourself—we are just about to unfold wide what is stored up; to abandon this conversation for that feast is not what is meant.”
translations.idiomatic: Young and low in rank, Dong Hui tried to withdraw when Dong Yun delayed the party. Dong Yun refused: “We came out to swap ideas with friends; you have humbled yourself to join us—this is the conversation worth having; skipping it for a banquet misses the point.”

sentences.zh: 」乃命解驂，禕等罷駕不行。

translations.literal: ” Then he ordered to unhitch the outer horses; Yi and the others called off the carriages and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He had the teams unhitched; Fei Yi and the rest cancelled the outing.

sentences.zh: 其守正下士，凡此類也。

translations.literal: His guarding rectitude and lowering himself to men of worth were in general of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity and respect for humble talent showed in countless such gestures.

sentences.zh: 〈《襄陽記》曰：董恢字休緒，襄陽人。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiangyang Record states: Dong Hui, courtesy name Xiuxu, a man of Xiangyang.”
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Xiangyang Record adds that Dong Hui, styled Xiuxu, came from Xiangyang.”

sentences.zh: 入蜀，以宣信中郎副費禕使吳。

translations.literal: He entered Shu as Faithful and Communicating Gentleman of the Household as deputy to Fei Yi on mission to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Shu he served as deputy to Fei Yi on embassy to Wu under the title faithful gentleman of the household.

sentences.zh: 孫權嘗大醉問禕曰：「楊儀、魏延，牧豎小人也。

translations.literal: Sun Quan once greatly drunk asked Yi, saying, “Yang Yi and Wei Yan are herd-boy petty men.”
translations.idiomatic: Once, drunk, Sun Quan said to Fei Yi, “Yang Yi and Wei Yan are nothing but rustics.”

sentences.zh: 雖嘗有鳴吠之益於時務，然既已任之，勢不得輕，若一朝無諸葛亮，必為禍亂矣。

translations.literal: Although they once had barking benefit for the affairs of the time, yet since already entrusted, the situation cannot be light; if one morning there were no Zhuge Liang, they would surely become calamity and disorder.”
translations.idiomatic: They may yap usefully for now, yet once raised to office they cannot be cast aside lightly—remove Zhuge Liang one morning and those two will tear Shu apart.”

sentences.zh: 諸君憒憒，曾不知防慮於此，豈所謂貽厥孫謀乎？

translations.literal: All of you are muddled and confused; you never thought to guard against this—can this be what is called leaving plans for one’s grandsons?”
translations.idiomatic: You gentlefolk stumble along blind to this danger—is this what it means to secure your children’s future?”

sentences.zh: 」禕愕然四顧視，不能即答。

translations.literal: ” Yi was dumbfounded, looked around on four sides, could not answer at once.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi stared about, speechless.

sentences.zh: 恢目禕曰：「可速言儀、延之不協起於私忿耳，而無黥、韓難御之心也。

translations.literal: Hui eyed Yi and said, “You can quickly say Yang Yi and Wei Yan’s discord arises from private resentment only, and they do not have the hearts of Qing Bu and Han Xin hard to control.”
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hui caught Fei Yi’s eye: “Say plainly that Yang Yi and Wei Yan feud out of private spite—they are no Ying Bu or Han Xin waiting to betray you.”

sentences.zh: 今方掃除強賊，混一區夏，功以才成，業由才廣，若捨此不任，防其後患，是猶備有風波而逆廢舟楫，非長計也。

translations.literal: Now we are just sweeping away the strong bandit, merging and uniting the region and summer; merit is completed by talent, enterprise is broadened by talent; if you discard these two and do not employ them, guarding against later trouble—it is like when wind and waves await yet you perversely abandon boats and oars; this is not a long-term plan.”
translations.idiomatic: You are crushing Wei and reuniting the realm; achievement rides on talent—discard capable men for fear of tomorrow and you might as well junk your boats while the seas still rage; that is no strategy.”

sentences.zh: 」權大笑樂。

translations.literal: ” Quan laughed greatly with delight.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮聞之，以為知言。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Liang heard it, he thought it speech of insight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang heard the story and pronounced it shrewd counsel.

sentences.zh: 還未滿三日，闢為丞相府屬，遷巴郡太守。

translations.literal: Before three days had passed since return, he was summoned as an aide in the chancellor’s office, promoted to Governor of Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Within three days of his return he entered the chancellor’s bureau and was named governor of Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：《漢晉春秋》亦載此語，不云董恢所教，辭亦小異，此二書俱出習氏而不同若此。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi examines: The Han–Jin Annals also records this saying; it does not say it was taught by Dong Hui; the wording is also slightly different; these two books both issue from the Xi clan yet differ thus.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that the Han–Jin Annals quotes the same exchange without crediting Dong Hui’s coaching and with slightly different wording—both stem from Xi Zuochi yet disagree.

sentences.zh: 本傳云「恢年少官微」，若已為丞相府屬，出作巴郡，則官不微矣。

translations.literal: The basic biography says ‘Hui was young and office low’; if he had already been chancellor’s office aide and gone out as Ba Commandery, then office would not be low.
translations.idiomatic: The main text calls Dong Hui young and lowly—yet if he had already served in the chancellor’s bureau before becoming governor of Ba, his rank was hardly humble.

sentences.zh: 以此疑習氏之言為不審的也。〉

translations.literal: By this I suspect Xi’s words are not precise and settled.〉
translations.idiomatic: On these grounds Pei Songzhi doubts Xi Zuochi’s account.〉

sentences.zh: 延熙六年，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanxi he was added General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: In 243 he received the additional title general who supports the state.

sentences.zh: 七年，以侍中守尚書令，為大將軍費禕副貳。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, as Palace Attendant he held concurrent Director of the Ministry, serving as Grand General Fei Yi’s deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In 244, while palace attendant, he acted as director of the secretariat and deputy to Grand General Fei Yi.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Yanxi (246).

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：時蜀人以諸葛亮、蔣琬、費禕及允為四相，一號四英也。〉

translations.literal: 〈The 《Huayang Guozhi》 states: At that time Shu people considered Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and Yun as the four chancellors, one title calling them the Four Heroes.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The 《Huayang Guozhi》 records that Shu folk ranked Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and Dong Yun as the “four chancellors,” or the Four Paragons.〉

sentences.zh: 陳祗代允為侍中，與黃皓互相表裡，皓始預政事。

translations.literal: Chen Zhi replaced Yun as Palace Attendant; with Huang Hao they mutually outside-and-inside; Hao began to participate in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi succeeded Dong Yun as palace attendant and colluded openly with Huang Hao, who now entered politics.

sentences.zh: 祗死後，皓從黃門令為中常侍、奉車都尉，操弄威柄，終至覆國。

translations.literal: After Zhi died, Hao went from Prefect of the Yellow Gates to Regular Palace Attendant and Commandant Who Conducts Chariots, wielded power and handles, ultimately reaching overturning the state.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Zhi died, Huang Hao rose from prefect of the Yellow Gates to regular attendant and chariot commandant, seized the levers of power, and helped bring down the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 蜀人無不追思允。

translations.literal: Shu people without exception recollected and longed for Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in Shu looked back on Dong Yun with longing.

sentences.zh: 及鄧艾至蜀，聞皓奸險，收閉，將殺之，而皓厚賂艾左右，得免。

translations.literal: When Deng Ai reached Shu, hearing Hao treacherous and dangerous, he seized and confined him, was about to kill him, but Hao heavily bribed Ai’s attendants and obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Ai entered Shu he jailed Huang Hao as a traitor and meant to execute him, but Huang Hao bought off Deng Ai’s staff and walked free.

sentences.zh: 呂乂字季陽，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Lü Yi, courtesy name Jiyang, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yi, styled Jiyang, came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 父常，送故將

translations.literal: His father Chang, accompanying the former general
translations.idiomatic: His father Lü Chang had gone as escort for a retiring general

translations.literal: (army)
translations.idiomatic: 〈manuscript gloss: “army”〉

sentences.zh: 劉焉入蜀，值王路隔塞，遂不得還。

translations.literal: Liu Yan entered Shu; it happened that royal roads were blocked and cut off; therefore he could not return.
translations.idiomatic: when Liu Yan marched into Shu; strife severed the highways home, and Lü Chang never returned.

sentences.zh: 乂少孤，好讀書鼓琴。

translations.literal: Yi was orphaned young; loved reading books and strumming the zither.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yi lost his father early and devoted himself to books and the qin.

sentences.zh: 初，先主定益州，置鹽府校尉，較鹽鐵之利，後校尉王連請乂及南陽杜祺、南鄉劉幹等並為典曹都尉。

translations.literal: At first, when the Former Lord pacified Yi Province, he established Salt Office Colonel, comparing salt and iron profits; afterward Colonel Wang Lian requested Yi and Nanyang Du Qi, Nanxiang Liu Gan, etc., together as Canon Bureau Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei took Yi Province he set up a salt monopoly; Colonel Wang Lian later named Lü Yi, Du Qi of Nanyang, Liu Gan of Nanxiang, and others commandants of the canon bureau.

sentences.zh: 乂遷新都、綿竹令，乃心隱卹，百姓稱之，為一州諸城之首。

translations.literal: Yi was promoted Prefect of Xindu and Mianzhu; he put his heart into relief and pity; the hundred surnames praised him—first among the various cities of one province.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Xindu and Mianzhu he ruled with compassion and ranked first among the province’s districts.

sentences.zh: 遷巴西太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted Governor of Brazil.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to governor of Brazil.

sentences.zh: 丞相諸葛亮連年出軍，調發諸郡，多不相救，乂募取兵五千人詣亮，慰喻檢制，無逃竄者。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhuge Liang for successive years led armies out; levies from the various commanderies often did not rescue one another; Yi recruited and took five thousand soldiers and sent them to Liang; comforting and explaining, inspecting and controlling—none fled or scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang’s yearly campaigns left commanderies unable to cover one another’s levies; Lü Yi raised five thousand men for him, kept order by encouragement and discipline, and lost no draftees to desertion.

sentences.zh: 徙為漢中太守，兼領督農，供繼軍糧。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Hanzhong, concurrently supervising agriculture, supplying continuing army grain.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hanzhong, he supervised farming and kept the army fed.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，累遷廣漢、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: When Liang died, he was successively promoted Governor of Guanghan and Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang’s death he rose through the governorships of Guanghan and Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡一都之會，戶口眾多，又亮卒之後，士伍亡命，更相重冒，姦巧非一。

translations.literal: Shu Commandery was one capital’s meeting place; households and registers were many; moreover after Liang died, soldiers and squads fled their registers; they mutually doubled and falsely claimed—crafty schemes were not of one kind.
translations.idiomatic: Shu commandery, thick with households, saw mass desertion and fraudulent census fraud after Zhuge Liang’s death.

sentences.zh: 乂到官，為之防禁，開喻勸導，數年之中，漏脫自出者萬馀口。

translations.literal: When Yi arrived at office, for them he set prohibitions; opened and explained and urged guidance; within several years, those who leaked out of hiding and gave themselves up exceeded ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yi barred further abuse, explained the law, and within a few years more than ten thousand people came back onto the rolls.

sentences.zh: 後入為尚書，代董允為尚書令，眾事無留，門無停賓。

translations.literal: Later he entered as Minister, replacing Dong Yun as Director of the Ministry—public affairs had nothing retained; gate had no halted guests.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as minister and succeeded Dong Yun as director of the secretariat; paperwork never stalled and petitioners never waited at his gate.

sentences.zh: 乂歷職內外，治身儉約，謙靖少言，為政簡而不煩，號為清能；

translations.literal: Yi held posts inner and outer; governed himself frugal and restrained; humble and quiet, little speech; his governance was simple without fuss—called clear and capable;
translations.idiomatic: In civil and military posts he lived plainly, spoke little, ran government with lean efficiency, and earned a reputation for integrity and competence;

sentences.zh: 然持法刻深，好用文俗吏，故居大官，名聲損於郡縣。

translations.literal: yet he held law harsh and deep; loved to use clerks versed in documents and common customs; therefore though dwelling in great office, reputation was diminished compared to when in commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: yet he enforced the code harshly and favoured petty clerks, so his prestige at the capital never matched his fame as a local governor.

sentences.zh: 延熙十四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yanxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of Yanxi (251).

sentences.zh: 子辰，景耀中為成都令。

translations.literal: His son Chen, during Jingyao served as Prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lü Chen became prefect of Chengdu during the Jingyao era.

sentences.zh: 辰弟雅，謁者。

translations.literal: Chen’s younger brother Ya, Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chen’s brother Lü Ya served as a herald.

sentences.zh: 雅清厲有文才，著格論十五篇。

translations.literal: Ya was clear and stern with literary talent; composed fifteen chapters of Model Discourses.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ya was austere and literate; he wrote fifteen chapters of the Model Discourses.

sentences.zh: 杜祺歷郡守監軍大將軍司馬，劉幹官至巴西太守，皆與乂親善，亦有當時之稱，而儉素守法，不及於乂。

translations.literal: Du Qi successively served as commandery governor, army supervisor, and Grand General’s major; Liu Gan’s office reached Governor of Brazil—all were intimate and good with Yi and also had contemporary praise, yet in frugality and plainness observing law they did not match Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qi rose through commandery posts to grand general’s chief of staff; Liu Gan reached Brazil—both were Lü Yi’s friends and noted men of their day, yet neither matched his frugal fidelity to the law.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: 【Appraisal】

sentences.zh: 評曰：董和蹈羔羊之素，劉巴履清尚之節，馬良貞實，稱為令士，陳震忠恪，老而益篤，董允匡主，義形於色，皆蜀臣之良矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Dong He trod the plainness of the lamb; Liu Ba stepped in the restraint of purity and elevation; Ma Liang was true and solid, called a fine gentleman; Chen Zhen was loyal and earnest, old yet more devoted; Dong Yun corrected the lord—righteousness took form in his expression—all were fine Shu ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The historian concludes: Dong He lived the simplicity praised in the Odes; Liu Ba kept an austere standard; Ma Liang was steadfast and rightly called a gentleman; Chen Zhen grew only more loyal with age; Dong Yun rebuked his sovereign with righteousness written on his face—these were Shu’s great servants.

sentences.zh: 呂乂臨郡則垂稱，處朝則被損，亦黃、薛之流亞矣。

translations.literal: Lü Yi when overseeing commanderies hung down praise; when at court suffered diminishment—also of the stream second to Huang and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yi shone in the provinces but lost lustre at court—very much in the line of Huang Ba and Xue Xuan, if one step below.
